svg.title: OLS vs Bayesian Linear Regression
svg.desc: OLS returns one coefficient estimate minimizing the residual sum of squares; Bayesian regression combines prior and data to give the full posterior of the coefficients and a posterior predictive distribution.
svg.text: Least Squares (OLS) vs Bayesian Linear Regression
Estimating one optimal coefficient vs inferring its whole posterior
The estimate is a single value
A penalty term is bolted on
One line — uncertainty lives only in the table
A bundle of lines drawn from the posterior
The line itself is a distribution — predictive uncertainty is visible
Reporting β: point estimate + standard error
You report a number and an interval — no probability statement is available
Reporting β: the whole posterior of β
Questions like "is the coefficient positive?" are answered directly
OLS finds the one coefficient vector minimizing the residual sum of squares.
Bayesian regression combines prior and data to obtain the whole coefficient distribution.
With a normal prior β~N(0, τ²I),
the posterior mean is the ridge estimator
Questions a point estimate cannot answer — P(β>0), predictive intervals — the posterior answers directly.
